column1: # enforcement.tsv (harbor#1028) — the enforcement matrix: one row per clause x moment x control, with the mode it runs in.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The constitution says "a mechanism that does not reach the moment of use is the same wish with more machinery",
# and nothing recorded which moment each rule reaches. A row joins a clause (policy/clauses.tsv) to the control that enforces it
# (standards/naming/controls.tsv), the moment that control binds and the mode it runs in; `judgment` is a moment, counted and never hidden.
# bin/policy-check.sh --enforcement judges the rows; --gen enforcement renders docs/policy/enforcement.md from them.
# COLUMNS  id clause moment mode control since promoted_by checkable_at later_why
#   moment        terms.tsv class moment, the closed set earliest first: write (admission) > session (injection) > commit (git hooks)
#                 > pr (the required CI check) > merge (backstop) > schedule (a registered check) > deploy (floor verify) > judgment
#   mode          shadow | warn | block, equal to the control's controls.tsv mode; - for judgment. Born shadow or warn
#   control       a controls.tsv id, or - for judgment. The red proof is that row's red_proof: joined, never copied here
#   since         the date this pair entered its present mode, or - when it predates the register
#   promoted_by   who promoted the pair to its present mode (a person), grandfathered (a block that predates the register), or -
#   checkable_at  the earliest moment the clause can be checked, a person's claim
#   later_why     why the pair binds later than checkable_at, or - when it does not
# PROMOTION is one cell in a person's PR, allowed only after the pair went red once (the control's red_proof names the suite that
# watched it) and ran 28 days in a lower mode. RETIREMENT deprecates the clause or control with a successor, never deletes the row.
